body.p: Status of the Application
By this Amendment, Claims 1-7 have been amended for clarity. No new subject matter has been added. Thus, Claims 1-7 are presently pending, with Claims 1, 6, and 7 being independent.
Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the claims in view of the presented amendments and accompanying remarks. Statement of Substance of Interview

On August 8, 2023, Applicant's undersigned representative held a telephonic interview with Examiners Alqaderi and Smith. Applicant and Applicant's representative appreciate the Examiners' willingness to conduct the interview and courtesies extended during the telephonic interview. Applicant submits this summary to record Applicant's representative's understanding of the substance of the interview. To the extent Applicant's understanding is incorrect, notice of such would be appreciated.

On the call, the parties discussed the rejection of Claim 1 and possible amendments for advancing prosecution. Although no formal agreement was reached as to the allowability of the claims, Applicant has amended independent Claims 1, 6, and 7 in a manner consistent with the suggestions made during the call and believed to advance prosecution in view of that discussion.
It is respectfully submitted that the instant STATEMVENT OF SUBSTANCE OF INTERVIEW complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. @@l.2 and 1.133 and MPEP §713.04.
Formalities
Applicant thanks the Examiner for confirming consideration of the references cited in the Information Disclosure Statements filed on July 7, 2021, and April 10, 2023.
Claims 1, 2, 6, and 7 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as purportedly being unpatentable over Ratnasingam (US 9,672,734) in view of Abe (US 2019/0113914).
Claims 3-5 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as purportedly being unpatentable over Ratnasingam and Abe, and in further view of Watanabe (US 2018/0105185).
Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the following reasons and discusses independent Claim 1 as an example.
Without any admissions, independent Claim 1 has been amended to recite:
A vehicle control device configured to control a vehicle, comprising:
an information provision device configured to provide information to a
driver of the vehicle;
a processor, during automated driving control of the vehicle, configured to: perform the automated driving control by automatically performing a
driving operation of the vehicle relating to a driving plan of the vehicle control device, the automated driving control comprising operations relating to at least one
of acceleration, steering, and braking, according to the driving plan;
provide, through the information provision device to the driver, a driving
event that is to occur at a point ahead in a direction of advance from a current point,
based on an automated driving plan;
judge a suitability of a driver driving operation corresponding to the driving
event being performed by the driver at a point before the point of the driving event;
and
provide the driver with judgment information indicating that the

driver not perform the driver driving operation, based on the judging of the suitability determining that performing the driver driving operation is unsuitable according to the driving plan being executed by the vehicle control
device.

At a minimum, the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe combination do not disclose, teach, or suggest "provid[ing] the driver with judgment information indicating that the driver not perform the driver driving operation, based on the judging of the suitability determining that performing the driver driving operation is unsuitable according to the driving plan being executed by the vehicle control device," as recited in Claim 1.

Ratnasingam is generally directed to "determining lane information in a road segment to drive a first vehicle to minimize travel time." Ratnasingam, Abstract. In particular, Ratnasingam discloses that "if there is sufficient data available to determine an optimum lane in fine mode to minimize travel time or to determine the rank order of the drivable lanes in the road segment for the first vehicle, then the system provides appropriate lane information to the driver of the first vehicle. By way of example only, the system may inform the driver about the other obstructing vehicle ahead in the road so that the driver of the first vehicle may perform an appropriate driving maneuver to minimize delay or go around the obstacle as appropriate." Id. at col. 20, li. 15-24. Ratnasingam further discloses that "the server system may not present the determined lane if changing of the lane is difficult, other vehicles in the determined lane are close to the first vehicle, other conditions including driver's cognitive load or driver state prevent such an action, and vehicle conditions." Id. at col. 21, li. 56-61.
That is, at best, Ratnasingam discloses not presenting appropriate lane information to the driver if changing to that lane is difficult.

To the extent the Office is attempting to equate the server system of Ratnasingam to the claimed "vehicle control device", Claim 1 recites "provid[ing] the driver with judgment information indicating that the driver not perform the driver driving operation, based on the judging of the suitability determining that performing the driver driving operation is unsuitable

according to the driving plan being executed by the vehicle control device." Ratnasingam does not disclose that its server system provides any such judgement information to the driver. Indeed, Ratnasingam discloses not presenting appropriate lane information to the driver if changing to that lane is difficult.
Consequently, Ratnasingam does not disclose, teach, or suggest at least the cited features recited in Claim 1.

The Office Action does not allege that Abe discloses the above-identified features of Claim 1 nor does Abe make up for at least these deficiencies of Ratnasingam. Thus, even assuming for the sake of argument only that the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe combination would have been proper, which Applicant does not concede, the proposed combination does not disclose, teach, or suggest all features recited in Claim 1.
In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 1 is patentable over the cited references and requests withdrawal of the rejection.

To the extent that independent Claims 6 and 7 recite features similar to the above-noted features of Claim 1, Applicant submits that Claims 6 and 7 are patentable for at least reasons similar to those discussed above with respect to Claim 1.

Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 2-5 are patentable due to their respective dependencies, as well as for their additional features. This should not be construed as an acquiescence to Examiner's interpretation of the claims, or reading of those claim elements on the prior art, and Applicant expressly reserves the right to establish the patentability of those additional claim limitations, should the need arise.

In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited.
